rationale: The construct — industry-ranked gross profitability times working-capital cash release — is economically the same object as generation-0's GrossProfitVsWorkingCapitalPressure (which paired gross profit with NEG working-capital accrual and produced a null alpha), differing mainly in data source and the omission of dp/cash/current-debt, so it risks being a re-run of a failed test while bundling the proven payables leg with two legs whose incremental content is untested.

Sign conventions are correct (RECCH/INVCH are already cash-flow-signed, and the balance-sheet fallback is negated consistently) and this cleanly isolates the asset side of the operating cycle against the payables-only winner, though it is an incremental component swap rather than a new mechanism and is close in spirit to the Sloan working-capital-accrual × gross-profitability composite already common in the quality literature.

This is a denominator rescaling of the archive's existing winner — exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against — and since cross-sectional ranking makes apalch/cogs versus apalch/at differ only by asset turnover, any change in results is an uninterpretable turnover interaction, compounded by the instability of cogs-scaling for low- or zero-COGS firms.

Profitability interacted with the stock of non-debt current liabilities scaled by assets is a direct rediscovery of Penman–Nissim operating liability leverage and is close to the inverse of the published net-operating-assets anomaly, so a positive result would most likely be attributed to those known effects rather than to a new cross-theme mechanism.

The tax leg is essentially a sign-flip of the already-tested TaxValidatedProfitability (pi × tax-accrual, which was flat), and bundling it with aoloch — an undefined residual "other assets and liabilities" catch-all with poor and format-dependent coverage — destroys the very mechanism discrimination the proposal claims as its justification.

Extending the working-capital cash flow to a five-year cumulative and the profitability leg to a three-year average makes a genuinely different economic claim (structural negative-working-capital business model versus one-year payment timing) rather than a cosmetic variant, though the reviewer should watch that the cumulative release does not simply proxy for the long-horizon net-operating-asset/asset-growth anomaly and that coverage does not collapse under the five-year cash-flow-item requirement.
